metadata.title: What Is Prompt Injection?
metadata.note: STEM/AI concept video on prompt injection. Real cited sources: OWASP LLM Top 10 2025 (#1 ranking, held since 2023); Cisco finding prompt injection weaknesses in 73% of audited production AI deployments (2026); HiddenLayer 2026 report (autonomous agents account for 1 in 8 reported AI breaches); cyberdesserts.com guide (direct vs indirect distinction, Anthropic dropping direct injection metric in Feb 2026 system card); Redfox Cybersecurity 2026 (indirect injection as dominant vector against GPT-4o and Claude-class agents).

beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Aishwarya from the Mycroft team. This video is about prompt injection — the attack that topped OWASP's list of the top ten risks in LLM applications in 2025, and hasn't moved since.

output: The attack at the top of OWASP's LLM Top 10 —

beats.narration_text: A text file on a webpage. A document a user uploads. An email an agent is asked to summarize. Any of these can carry instructions the model will follow — instructions that weren't put there by the developer.

props.greeting: A webpage. A document. An email.
props.runningText: any of these can carry instructions…
output: instructions the developer never put there

beats.narration_text: Method: there are two real, distinct forms. Direct injection is when a user types adversarial instructions straight into the interface — ignore your previous instructions and do this instead. Indirect injection is far more dangerous: the attacker's instructions arrive in external data the model retrieves or processes — a web page, a document, an email — not through any user-facing input at all.

beats.role_note: why it's different from SQL injection
beats.narration_text: Traditional injection attacks exploit poor input validation in code. Prompt injection is different in kind: the model follows natural language instructions by design. There is no separator between data and instruction — it's all text, processed together. That's not a bug in a specific model; it's a structural property of how language models work.

This isn't theoretical. Cisco found prompt injection weaknesses in 73% of audited production AI deployments in 2026. OWASP ranks it at the top of their LLM Top 10 specifically because indirect attacks scale. HiddenLayer's 2026 report found autonomous agents account for one in eight reported AI breaches.

The real severity scales with what the model can do. A model that can only talk produces text. A model wired to send email, query databases, or execute code turns a successful injection into a real-world action. The instruction in the malicious document doesn't just change the response — it takes the action.

Your turn. If you're building an AI-powered app that reads external content — documents, emails, web pages — ask what the worst instruction that content could contain would do. If the answer is something you'd never want the app to do, that's the injection surface you need to think about.
